subject: Dedicated deployment: burst orchestration, multiplexing and SLA hedge
messages:
From: Sophie Grant <sophie@helium.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Dan Li <dan.li@helium.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity + burst plan for Q1 launch

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are planning a limited public beta for HeliumAI on Jan 15 and expect a highly spiky traffic profile: inferred peaks 5–8x baseline for short windows (2–10 minutes) when certain features go viral.

We want Redwood Dedicated but need clarity on:
- how burst credits and shoulder pools work in practice (eviction, prewarm, throttling),
- what autoscale windows you recommend for mission-critical routes vs background inferencing,
- any SLA/credits implications if burst capacity is unavailable, and
- an example sizing plan tied to our forecast (we'll attach baseline traffic).

Can you share a short playbook and a recommended configuration we can include in our procurement/ops runbook? Procurement will need a clear heads-up on potential overage triggers.

Appreciate it — Sophie

--
Sophie Grant
Head of Platform
HeliumAI
@sophiegrant
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sophie Grant <sophie@helium.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T11:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + burst plan for Q1 launch

Hi Sophie —

Great question and timely. I pulled together an initial playbook and a sample burst matrix (attached) that maps forecasted traffic to: dedicated slab sizing, shoulder reserve pools, prewarm cadence, and eviction priority. High level:

- Short spikes (<=10 minutes, up to 8x): we recommend a dedicated shoulder pool of ~25% of baseline with prewarm enabled for the two highest-traffic routes. That covers most 2–10 minute viral events with <200ms tail impact.
- Sustained surges (>30 minutes): route to a transient slab (ephemeral) with proportional backfill; will require explicit commit or credits depending on duration.
- Eviction policy: priority weight = {online payments, auth, inference_high_quality, background}. We can tune weights per your business rules.
- SLA hedge: we propose an addendum that preserves your latency SLOs up to the shoulder threshold and a fallback model variant (smaller quantized) beyond that. The draft SLA addendum is attached.

I've looped in Ben and Karthik to comment on the eviction/queue-weight design and the practical operator knobs (credits, prewarm timings). If this aligns, we'll convert the attachments into a formal exhibit for procurement.

Attachments: Helium_Dedicated_Requirements_20261201.pdf, burst_matrix_v1.xlsx, SLA_addendum_draft_20261202.docx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T14:23:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + burst plan for Q1 launch

Marissa / Sophie —

Quick operator notes to add to the playbook:

1) Eviction & queue weight: we recommend a two-tier queue with configurable decay windows. Short-lived spikes should bleed first from lower-priority background queues. If you expect sudden spikes tied to a product event (campaigns), we can temporarily bump weights for those user-facing routes via an API call from your ops runbook.

2) Prewarm strategy: trigger prewarm jobs 90s before expected window when we have an external signal (CDN event, campaign webhook). Without a signal, we use predictive prewarm heuristics based on trailing 15m traffic. Prewarm cost is small vs cold-started ephemeral slabs.

3) Credit accounting: we suggest a capped burst credit pool that auto-refills monthly with top-ups on large sustained events. We'll include an example amortization table in the next version of the matrix.

I'll add a column to burst_matrix_v1.xlsx for "operator triggers" and "runbook API calls."

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + burst plan for Q1 launch

Adding sizing numbers (based on Helium's baseline sample in the PDF):

- Baseline GPUs: 12 A100-equivalent for production slab (expected steady qps ~6k tokens/s).
- Shoulder pool: reserve 3 GPUs for short spikes (25% headroom).
- Ephemeral slab for >30m surges: add blocks of 4 GPUs; eviction/grace period of 10m before billing shift to committed pool.

Operational knobs to call out in the exhibit:
- max_preheat_instances = 2 per route
- preheat_lead = 90s
- credit_threshold_alert = 60% remaining
- auto-burst-fallback-model = "gpt-small-q4" (quantized)

I'll update the burst_matrix_v1.xlsx with these values and a sample hourly cost delta. We should also propose a one-time implementation window (2 weeks) for instrumentation (webhook + ops playbook).

Karthik
Sr. Infra Product, Redwood Inference
From: Sophie Grant <sophie@helium.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Dan Li <dan.li@helium.ai>, procurement@helium.ai
Date: 2026-12-03T16:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity + burst plan for Q1 launch

Thanks everyone — this is exactly what we needed. A few quick confirmations before procurement signs:

- Helium accepts the recommended shoulder pool (3 GPUs) and the prewarm cadence.
- We'd like the eviction priority list preserved as-is and a short runbook snippet for triggering prewarm via our campaign webhook.
- Please produce the export-ready exhibit (with the amortized credit table and explicit overage alert thresholds) so procurement can review cost impact.

If you can get the exhibit and the updated spreadsheet to me by EOD Monday (2026-12-06), procurement will aim to circulate redlines the following week.

I'll attach any procurement templates as soon as Dan forwards them.

Best,
Sophie
